notes:
User is organizing their garage and bookshelf this weekend and is making strong progress with tidying. They have maintained a daily tidying routine for four weeks and are proud of its positive impact on their apartment. Encourage and remember this accomplishment.

Garage priorities: purge and categorize clutter, especially tools, sports equipment, old furniture, and an unused desk they are eager to donate, sell, recycle, or responsibly dispose of. They plan to replace the desk with a dedicated workstation for daily tidying, keeping supplies there rather than on the kitchen counter. Planned supplies include all-purpose cleaners, disinfectants, dusters, paper towels, a cordless vacuum, and a microfiber mop. They recently began using an all-natural bathroom cleaner that works well on soap scum and mildew and like it.

They plan to use stackable bins, shelving, and labels. Useful guidance: use “Keep / Donate-Sell / Recycle / Toss”; apply the “one-touch rule” by making an immediate decision and assigning each item a home; use a dated “maybe” box; group similar items; keep frequently used supplies accessible and infrequent items higher or farther back; maximize vertical space; measure before buying bins; choose durable, stable, easy-to-clean bins; and clearly label bins and shelf locations. They chose a Brother P-Touch label maker; durable outdoor/laminated labels would suit garage use.

For the bookshelf, they particularly like categorizing and grouping similar books. Other ideas: donate damaged/unwanted books, keep favorites or frequently read books accessible, create a “to-read” section, use bookends/risers, avoid overcrowding, and label shelves rather than every book with a consistent style.

For cleaning supplies, they are deciding between organization by room or product type. A recommended hybrid is first by type (all-purpose, glass, disinfectant, etc.), then by room/area, reducing duplication while making supplies easy to locate. Suggest labeled bins, a caddy or divided bucket for portability, frequent items at easy reach, and safe storage away from children and pets.
